results.title: AITA for getting mad at my wife that we spent way too much time with her family friends on our honeymoon?

refined: The narrator is in Belize on his honeymoon, having married on March 9.
The wife's parents offered to pay 100% of the honeymoon and let the couple stay in their Belize house for three weeks if the couple had a small, inexpensive ceremony.
According to the narrator, he later learned there was also an expectation to visit five sets of the parents' Belize friends, which he had not been told about.
By yesterday they had reached the fourth set of friends; the first three visits went fine, including with friends Rod and Pete.
At the fourth couple's home, the hosts were older and agitated, the house was extremely hot, and they complained extensively about personal and family problems.
The visit lasted nearly six hours without the hosts offering drinks.
When the narrator asked for water, he found the kitchen and dishes filthy and took a hot bottled water, which angered the husband.
After leaving, the narrator told his wife the visit was one of the most miserable experiences of his life and called the hosts miserable.
His wife said those hosts were two of her dearest friends and accused him of being ungrateful to her parents for paying for the trip.
The narrator said he wished the expectation to spend so long with such friends had been clearly stated as a condition of the honeymoon.
His wife became angry, called Rod and Pete to pick her up, and left.
He has not seen her since the previous evening, and his texts to her are not being delivered.
He does not know how to get to Rod and Pete's house and is waiting by his phone, unsure what to do.
